wev.us-midterms-2026.n: US midterm elections: Democrats take both chambers
wev.us-midterms-2026.t: In the midterm elections of 3 November 2026 the Democrats won control of the House and the Senate, ending the Republican trifecta. By the morning of 4 November they led the House 228–139 with 19 seats gained and had flipped seven Senate seats for a 54–44 majority, with Alaska and Mississippi still uncalled; James Talarico’s defeat of Ken Paxton in Texas was the party’s first statewide win there in more than 30 years. Trump said: ‘I have total veto power, so they have to come to us.’
wev.nk-missiles-nov-2026.n: North Korea fires missiles into the East Sea
wev.nk-missiles-nov-2026.t: South Korea’s military detected several missiles fired on the morning of 4 November from the Sondok area, about 170 km north-east of Pyongyang, toward the East Sea; KCNA said the North had tested a new air-defence missile and rehearsed a fire strike. No talks with Washington are announced, and the FBI blames Pyongyang for the theft of more than $6bn in cryptocurrency from Binance (Stars and Stripes, 5 November).
wev.myanmar-byelections.t: Myanmar’s election commission announced on 6 November by-elections on 4 April 2027 in 39 constituencies, about a third of them in areas of Sagaing, Mandalay and Chin where voting was cancelled for security reasons during the phased general election of December 2025 and January 2026 that made coup leader Min Aung Hlaing president. Aung San Suu Kyi remains detained and her party dissolved; ACLED counts more than 100,000 deaths since the 2021 coup.
wev.cop31-antalya.t: The UN climate conference COP31 runs from 9 to 20 November 2026 at the Antalya Expo Center under a Turkish presidency, with Australia’s Chris Bowen as president of negotiations and a leaders’ summit on 11–12 November. The opening plenary on 9 November adopted a standalone Climate Finance Work Programme demanded by developing countries, over EU objections, and dropped separate agenda items on tripling adaptation finance and on climate-related trade measures; UNEP puts developing countries’ adaptation needs at $305bn a year by 2035.
wev.abu-dhabi-talks.n: Ukraine, Russia and the US talk in Abu Dhabi
wev.abu-dhabi-talks.t: Ukraine, Russia and the United States held their first talks since February on 10–11 November 2026 in Abu Dhabi, without Germany, France or Britain. Russia’s delegation head Vladimir Medinsky said he would be satisfied ‘only when we win and sign a peace agreement on our terms’; Russia demands territory and a NATO pull-back from members that joined after 1997, Ukraine wants an Article 5-style guarantee, and the sides agreed to exchange at least 1,000 prisoners each (Al Jazeera, 13 November).
wev.china-pacific-drills.t: In early November 2026 China massed more than 100 naval and coast guard vessels across the western Pacific and around Taiwan in unannounced drills larger than ‘Justice Mission 2025’, with all three theatre commands, the Liaoning carrier group east of the Philippines, simulated attacks on cities and a submarine-launched intercontinental missile fired from the Yellow Sea into the Chinese mainland. About 70 vessels remained inside the first island chain on 13 November; Taipei called it ‘silent intimidation’ before the APEC summit.
wev.sudan-khuwai.n: Sudan’s army takes al-Khuwai in West Kordofan
wev.sudan-khuwai.t: The Sudanese Armed Forces took al-Khuwai, a main town of West Kordofan, on 13 November 2026, weeks after breaking the RSF siege of El Obeid with allied Darfur forces; the capture opens routes toward Babnusa and North Darfur. The RSF still holds al-Nuhud, parts of South Kordofan and all five Darfur states, and Al Jazeera puts the war’s toll at about 150,000 dead and more than 14 million displaced.
wev.starship-flight-15.t: SpaceX’s Starship Flight 15 lifted off from Starbase, Texas, at 5.47 pm EST on 13 November 2026; the Super Heavy booster logged a low-fuel alarm, diverted to the Gulf and was destroyed by its flight-termination system, but Ship 42 deployed 26 Starlink V3 satellites, flew 14 orbits in nearly a day and at 4.18 pm EST on 14 November was caught by the launch tower’s ‘chopstick’ arms, the first catch of a Ship returning from orbit (Space.com).
wev.asean-manila.t: The ASEAN summit opened in Manila on 15 November 2026 under Philippine chairmanship, with Brazil’s Lula and Canada’s Mark Carney among the guests, tariffs and the Middle East on the agenda and the South China Sea code of conduct said to be 80% negotiated; nearly 20,000 police were deployed and about 200 protesters clashed with police on the first day. Trump arrived on 17 November for the first Quad meeting of his second term with India, Japan and Australia before flying to Shenzhen (The Star, 15 November; RFA, 18 November).
wev.houthis-bab-al-mandeb.n: Houthis take the Bab al-Mandeb coast
wev.houthis-bab-al-mandeb.t: On 15 November 2026 Yemen’s Southern Armed Forces announced a ‘repositioning’ away from Dhubab airport and the Bab al-Mandeb area in western Taiz to defend Aden and relieve besieged Taiz; the Houthis claimed to have expelled them and by 16 November had advanced about 50 miles along the Gulf of Aden coast, to within reported reach of Aden. Saudi Arabia replaced its Joint Forces commander the same day as its coalition intercepted Houthi drones over Riyadh and Mecca.
wev.ny-sales-nov-2026.n: New York’s November sales: records for Van Gogh, Kandinsky and Kusama
wev.ny-sales-nov-2026.t: Sotheby’s opened the marquee week on 16 November 2026 with $378.7m across two evening sales and a $15m record for Yayoi Kusama, who died in August; Christie’s 20th-century sale on 17 November made $627m with fees, with Kandinsky’s Betonte Ecken (1923) at $85.8m, a record, Klimt’s Litzlbergkeller at $82.3m and a Jeff Koons-consigned group at $104.7m. On 18 November Van Gogh’s Blossoming Chestnut Trees (1890), its Nazi-era provenance settled a day earlier, sold at Sotheby’s for $190.4m with fees to William Acquavella, a record for the artist though below its $180m estimate on the hammer.
wev.gaza-central-push.n: Israel’s first ground push in Gaza since the ceasefire
wev.gaza-central-push.t: On 18 November 2026 Israeli tanks advanced east of the Nuseirat camp and north of Bureij in central Gaza in the first broad ground operation since the October 2025 ceasefire; the army said it was removing a threat to its forces at the ‘Yellow Line’, hospital officials reported three Palestinians killed and residents of Maghazi and Bureij fled without an evacuation order. Hamas called it a flagrant violation, and the Board of Peace had warned the truce faced collapse.
wev.hegseth-caracas.n: The US and Venezuela restore military ties
wev.hegseth-caracas.t: US Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth visited Caracas on 18 November 2026, met acting President Delcy Rodríguez and signed an agreement restoring military ties covering training, intelligence sharing and equipment, calling Venezuela ‘a compliant security partner’ ten months after the 48-minute operation that seized Nicolás Maduro. No election date is set; AP counts at least 240 killed in US strikes on alleged drug boats since September 2025.
wev.tripp-armenia.n: Armenia says the TRIPP corridor enters implementation
wev.tripp-armenia.t: Prime Minister Nikol Pashinyan said on 18 November 2026 that the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity, a 42 km road, rail and pipeline corridor across southern Armenia linking Azerbaijan to Nakhchivan and on to Turkey, is ‘entering the practical implementation phase’, and that the southern Armenian–Azerbaijani border must now be delimited; he and Ilham Aliyev reaffirmed their agreements at a meeting in Dublin (Interfax).
wev.apec-shenzhen-trilateral.n: APEC in Shenzhen and the Trump–Xi–Putin summit
wev.apec-shenzhen-trilateral.t: The 33rd APEC leaders’ meeting ran in Shenzhen on 18–19 November 2026; Xi Jinping met Trump at the foot of Air Force One. On 19 November Xi chaired the first three-way summit with Trump and Putin at Kylin Villa, which issued a ‘peace declaration’ pledging talks on nuclear risks and proliferation, stable energy flows and closer cooperation, and criticising the International Criminal Court; it made no mention of Ukraine or Iran, though Trump pressed Xi on the war and said Tehran cannot have a nuclear weapon (Al Jazeera).
wev.haiti-martissant.t: On 19 November 2026 Haiti’s armed forces and police, with a task force that included Erik Prince’s Vectus Global, launched an operation to clear gangs from Martissant, the western tip of Port-au-Prince that controls Route 2 to the south and has been in gang hands for more than five years; police said 34 suspected gang members were killed, a figure not independently verified. El Salvador has about 2,500 troops in the country and the UN-backed Gang Suppression Force works in Tabarre, Artibonite and on Route 5 (AP).
